quote: Section 9.2(a) covers *all* breaches of Seller's representations and warranties. Read as written, the 10%-of-Purchase-Price cap (§ 9.4(a)) and the $184,000 basket (§ 9.4(b)) apply only to covenant breaches ... Every rep-and-warranty claim—whether fundamental or ordinary—is uncapped and has no deductible. ... The escrow is only $1,840,000, but under § 9.6 Buyer can recover directly from Seller above the escrow. Marrowind's total indemnification exposure is theoretically unlimited. ... Amend § 9.4(c) to: "The limitations set forth in Section 9.4(a) and Section 9.4(b) shall not apply to any claim under Section 9.2(a) arising from a breach of a Fundamental Representation, or to any claim arising from fraud."
reason: The memo meets each part of the criterion. It names APA §9.4(c) as the problem and explains that it removes the §9.4(a) 10% cap for every §9.2(a) claim, covering all representations and not only fundamental ones. It states that Marrowind's exposure is uncapped and goes beyond the $1,840,000 escrow. It recommends narrowing the carve-out to Fundamental Representations and fraud. The memo does not suggest capping the remaining uncapped claims at the Purchase Price, which the ledger mentions, but the criterion offers that only as an example and does not require it.
